subject.title: fix(gateway): regenerate native hook descriptors when relay unavailable after restart

question: Should pre-invocation Codex native-relay unavailability fall through to generic OpenClaw before-tool policy, or must approval remain fail-closed until the relay is refreshed or re-registered?
rationale: Both approaches can address the user-visible outage, but they establish different native-tool enforcement boundaries, and tests alone cannot determine the intended security policy.

options.title: Accept guarded fallback
options.body: Require exact-head live proof that the generic policy path enforces the same relevant checks, then accept fallback only when the current tool call was never invoked by the relay.

options.title: Require relay refresh
options.body: Keep unavailable approval fail-closed and repair or regenerate the active relay registration before retrying policy evaluation.

options.title: Keep current fail-closed behavior
options.body: Decline the fallback and retain the existing hard block until a different self-healing design is available.

recommendation.title: Accept guarded fallback
recommendation.body: Require exact-head live proof that the generic policy path enforces the same relevant checks, then accept fallback only when the current tool call was never invoked by the relay.

likelyOwner.reason: The guarded no-policy fallback commit is the clearest existing merged contract for unavailable native-hook behavior.
